test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 01 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A dealer allowed a 73\% discount on an article and was still able to manage a 56\% profit. Find the ratio of the cost price to listed price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for **Ratio of Cost Price (CP) to Marked Price (MP)**:

**CP : MP** = (100 − **Discount%**) : (100 + **Profit%**)

**CP : MP** = (100 − 73) : (100 + 56)

**CP : MP** = 27 : 156 = 9 : 52

**∴ The correct answer is 9 : 52.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Discount** = 73%

**Profit** = 56%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/632d6338c602b3639d8aac0c30f7ddffd4e3296af6cded5527bda7a9300b3d85.png] 

Let **Listed Price (MP)** = 100 units

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = MP − Discount = 100 − 73 = 27 units

⇒ **Profit** is 56%, so **SP** = CP × (156/100)

⇒ 27 = **CP** × 1.56

⇒ **CP** = 27 ÷ 1.56 = 2700 ÷ 156

⇒ **Ratio CP : MP** = (2700/156) : 100

⇒ **Ratio** = 2700 : 15600 = 27 : 156

⇒ Dividing by 3: 9 : 52

**∴ The correct answer is 9 : 52.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Selling Price

**Selling Price (SP)** = **Marked Price (MP)** × (100 − **Discount%**)/100.

Cost Price and Selling Price

**Selling Price (SP)** = **Cost Price (CP)** × (100 + **Profit%**)/100.

Successive Discounts

Total Discount for two successive discounts d₁ and d₂ = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100.</p
